highlights.title: Lenovo confirms Legion Go issues after gamers report bricked devices
highlights.summary: When a company's software update turns your computer into a useless brick, should fixes be free? Framework, the modular computer startup, apparently thinks so. But it's not clear that computing giant Lenovo will go that far.
body: I installed Lenovo’s forbidden BIOS and my Legion Go lived. You might be less lucky.

Three weeks after a Redditor presented a nearly $300 repair bill for their handheld gaming PC — among other reports of damage and high repair bills — the company is breaking its silence. It says, in short: try holding down the power button longer, and if that fails, contact customer support.

Lenovo is aware that some Legion Go devices may experience a blank screen during installation of BIOS version V42. BIOS V42 was not distributed through Windows Update or Legion Space, and Lenovo has removed the update from its support website while we continue our validation work. Users who have successfully completed the V42 update should not need to take further action at this time.

If a device encounters a blank screen during V42 installation, users may try pressing and holding the power button for approximately 10 seconds, waiting approximately one minute, and then powering the device on again. If the device does not resume normal operation, customers should contact Lenovo Support for further assistance.
points: When a company's software update turns your computer into a useless brick, should fixes be free?
But it's not clear that computing giant Lenovo will go that far.

highlights.summary: Cole Palmer was back to his best to get Xabi Alonso's Chelsea career off to a winning start in a chaotic 3-2 victory at Fulham on Monday Night Football.
body: The Blues' attacking trio of Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers looked every bit the most potent in the Premier League as all three scored in a game where entertainment reigned and defending was an afterthought.

Palmer, finally injury-free and all the better for a summer off from England's World Cup campaign, scored one and made another in the kind of performance he had found so difficult to reproduce last season.
If his confidence on the pitch was not evidence enough, his response when Sky Sports asked how ready he was for the new season was emphatic. "Did you not watch the game?"
It took just 31 seconds for him to lay down a marker by teeing up an opener for Joao Pedro - himself refreshed after his surprise Brazil omission. The front three never looked back from there.

highlights.title: Newegg Has the Least Overpriced 32GB of DDR5 6000MHz CL 30 Desktop Memory
highlights.summary: RAM is expensive and there's no way of getting around it. If you're going to upgrade your existing memory or build a PC from scratch, you just have to accept the fact that your budget needs to accommodate for today's RAM prices. Still not fazed?
body: For a limited time, you can pick up 32GB (2x16GB) of the V-COLOR Manta XSky DDR5-6000MHz CL30 Desktop Memory for $369.59 with free shipping. You'll need to be signed into your AliExpress account and then click on the link to see the pricing. If the page says it's not available for shipping, reload a couple of times (sometimes it's actually out of stock, sometimes it's just a glitch). If you buy it directly from Newegg's site, you're going to pay $420 for the same RAM.

V-COLOR is a well known memory brand. The Manta XSky DDR5 RAM in particular uses SK Hynix ICs, which are considered one of the best memory chips you can get. The RAM is meant for AMD systems (although it could work with Intel) since it's preloaded with an AMD EXPO overclocking profile and not Intel XMP. The rated speed of 6,000MHz and CAS latency of 30 is considered the sweet spot for AMD CPUs. Unless you're going after benchmark leaderboards (and hve a LOT of disposable cash), RAM with higher speeds and lower memory latencies are wasted on gaming builds.
Is it better to wait for RAM to go down in price? Unless you're willing to wait a few years, probably not.

highlights.title: AI is hitting entry-level jobs hardest, Stanford study finds
highlights.summary: For years, AI industry watchers of all stripes have been warning of a coming jobs apocalypse driven by ultra-intelligent AI systems that will be able to replicate most human tasks more cheaply.
body: The August 2026 edition of “Canaries in the Coal Mine? Six Facts about the Recent Employment Effects of Artificial Intelligence” updates and revises a paper of the same name published last year with fresh data and refined statistics. In that update, the Stanford researchers find the employment trends they identified for entry-level workers last year are persisting and expanding. Specifically, employment levels for workers aged 22 to 25 in the most “AI-exposed” occupations are now 19 percent below those of their peers in fields less exposed to AI disruption.

To determine those numbers, the researchers used a large subsample of the anonymized, high-frequency payroll data regularly aggregated by HR management company ADP. The team then rated each occupation’s “exposure” to AI disruption using both a potential labor market impact gauge established by previous researchers (we took a somewhat critical look at that previous research earlier this year) and the Anthropic Economic Index, which looks at how various occupations actually use the Claude model in their everyday work (Google released a similar report based on occupational Gemini usage last month).

highlights.title: Situational Awareness, star AI hedge fund that nearly imploded, now being probed by the SEC
highlights.summary: The AI hedge fund went from "the talk of Wall Street" to "subject of federal subpoenas" faster than you can say "diversify your portfolio."
body: Situational Awareness, the AI focused hedge fund that was Wall Street’s fleeting obsession, is having a very bad month.

The company, led by twentysomething OpenAI alum Leopold Aschenbrenner, went all-in on a variety of AI investments and, for a period, enjoyed phenomenal growth. Then, at the end of July, a downturn in AI stocks erased billions of dollars in value at the firm. Now, federal regulators are reportedly probing the company as well.

The New York Times reports that the Securities and Exchange Commission has been subpoenaing banks that did business with the hedge fund. The subpoenas focus on the banks that supervised the fund’s trading and that channeled funding to support it, the outlet says.
The government reportedly warned the banks to “preserve any information” about the hedge fund, though it noted that Situational Awareness has not been accused of any wrongdoing.

highlights.title: “We killed Clash Royale!”: What Supercell learned from failed updates
highlights.summary: Clash Royale has had its ups and downs over the years with some major backlash from players and fans over updates. During a session at Gamescom Dev titled 'Clash Royale: Lessons from the players', Supercell game design lead James Back and community manager Emilia Russell shared their insights from…
body: Russell noted, though, that even the harshest and most critical feedback comes from a place of caring about a game and players wanting the best for it - even if it’s not always given in the most clear or constructive way.

First, they opened up on the Season Shop. Described as “one of the most popular reward systems in the game”, it allowed players to spend Season Tokens on cards and other items. In March 2025, Supercell decided to remove it.

Back said it was for good reason. The team felt it only benefitted a small group of core players and they wanted to put the rewards somewhere more accessible to more players. The update worked at achieving that goal. The percentage of monthly active users earning any common wild cards grew from 59.8% in March 2025 to 67.4% in April 2025.
But due to the Season Shop’s popularity, its sudden removal resulted in “broken trust” and negative sentiment. The average daily rating on Google Play plummeted.

highlights.title: Problems brewing for the proper pint as Camra membership falls
highlights.summary: Cost of living has hit campaign group while multinationals are threatening to squeeze out independent breweries. For centuries, the wooden real ale pump has been the hallmark of a good British boozer.
body: Real ale is a traditional draught cask beer, a “living” product that is produced and stored in its cask. It differs from a cold, fizzy lager, in which the yeast is killed and carbon dioxide is added. Real ale contains live yeast so it continues fermenting until it is served.

Outside the Devonshire pub in Soho, central London, there is an ever-present horde of drinkers downing pints of Guinness, a stout made by the multinational company Diageo. But the landlord and co-owner Oisín Rogers says: “Real ale is all I drink.”

He says: “It is a properly handmade British product produced in exactly the same way it has been for centuries. It has never been industrialised like some of the other drinks that are for sale in bars in London.” His favourite tipple, is, appropriately, a pint of Landlord, made by the family-owned Timothy Taylor brewery in Keighley, West Yorkshire.

Tom Stainer, Camra’s chief executive, says independent breweries are facing unfair competition from multinationals. If you walk into a pub on the high street, you are often confronted with the same few beers, most of which are made by the same large companies, Stainer says.

highlights.title: Data centers become "killer application" for new power transformer tech
highlights.summary: Data centers have become the largest driver of surging electricity demand that is straining US power grids. But the AI data center boom has also accelerated investment in a technology that could provide a silver lining for everyone—solid-state power transformers that replace industrial-age…
body: Power grids currently rely on conventional transformer technology that is painstakingly assembled by hand and has a fundamental design dating back to the 1880s. Two copper wire coils manually wound around a steel core create electromagnetic fields that help step up voltage levels of alternating current electricity for long-distance transmission or step down voltage levels for the electricity use of homes and businesses. The largest power transformers cannot be mass-manufactured but are instead custom-built for each utility company’s electrical substations.

Manufacturing constraints, coupled with the scramble to upgrade US power infrastructure, have meant utility companies and other customers must wait up to several years for delivery of new power transformers. That is not only a problem for expanding power grid infrastructure to support growing electricity demand, but also delays the process of replacing aging power transformers.

highlights.title: Generating scenarios for extreme events, without extreme data
highlights.summary: A new algorithm learns to anticipate the unprecedented scenarios that critical infrastructure and global supply chains are least prepared for.
body: Images for download on the MIT News office website are made available to non-commercial entities, press and the general public under a Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial No Derivatives license. You may not alter the images provided, other than to crop them to size. A credit line must be used when reproducing images; if one is not provided below, credit the images to "MIT."
Can a city’s seawall stand up to a blockbuster storm? Will a region’s power grid hold against record-breaking heat? And can a town’s fire-fighting resources contain a major wildfire?

To answer these questions, communities will first need to know how such extreme events could unfold. How far is a wildfire likely to spread? How much of a region might a storm impact? How long could a heat wave last?

But extreme events are notoriously difficult to anticipate. By their nature, they are outliers. In the history of record keeping, extreme events are sporadic and rare. Yet most methods that assess a region’s risk depend on extreme events of the past to characterize even more extreme, worst-case scenarios in the future.

highlights.title: Poulter undecided about LIV Golf future
highlights.summary: Ian Poulter hasn't made up his mind on whether he will continue to play on LIV Golf next season, but hopes the league could continue to operate next year, amid concerns over its funding.
body: Alongside his Majestiks GC team-mate Lee Westwood, Poulter was among some of the first players to join the rebel league back in 2022.

But as LIV Golf concluded its 2026 season in Indianapolis last weekend, Poulter took to Instagram to explain he was undecided if he would play on the tour into next year, adding that he was 'proud' of what LIV has achieved.

"This final phase has been tough and none of us knows exactly what comes next," the five-time Ryder Cup champion said. "My thoughts are especially with the businesses and suppliers still owed money. Some are small businesses and I sincerely hope those situations are dealt with properly and quickly.
"It would be a real shame if LIV 2.0 doesn't happen. There are players who would love a strong global platform to play on and countries and fans who want us back.

highlights.title: The Witcher 3 Songs of the Past Expansion Confirmed to Include More Gwent, and Everyone Is Already Celebrating
highlights.summary: CD Projekt Red has confirmed The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt 's upcoming Songs of the Past expansion will come with more Gwent, and card game lovers are already celebrating. The Witcher 3 earned a lot of praise when it launched back in 2015.
body: "In Gwent, gamers clash with friends in fast-paced duels that combine skill-based play with bluffing, and careful deck construction," an official description from CD Projekt Red says. "The game is played over a best-of-three series of rounds, as players unleash their hand by slinging spells and diverse units with special abilities, and use clever tricks to deceive their opponents."

CD Projekt Red's in-universe card game first launched within the third installment in its Witcher series before being transformed into a standalone spinoff in 2017 and a real-life tabletop experience in 2025. It's a formula others have unsuccessfully attempted to mimic, but few have managed to stand the test of time quite like Gwent. That's probably exactly why it will be making a comeback when the developer returns to The Witcher 3 with its Songs of the Past expansion in 2027.

CD Projekt Red community and social media manager Marcin Łukaszewski teased the return of the fan-favorite side activity when replying to a player on X/Twitter. When the fan said they hoped more Gwent would be included in the surprise expansion, Łukaszewski offered a simple reply: "Confirmed!"

highlights.title: Taylor Swift Recalls How ‘I Knew You Were Trouble’ Was Written As a ‘Really Sad Ballad’ in Grammy Museum Conversation Video
highlights.summary: Taylor Swift opened up about the process of writing and recording her 2012 hit “I Knew You Were Trouble,” revealing that it was initially penned as a “really sad ballad” before she was encouraged to incorporate dubstep.
body: Swift reflected on the song’s creation during a Q&A at the Grammy Museum in Los Angeles last week, moderated by Recording Academy CEO Harvey Mason Jr. The conversation, held as part of the Museum’s Icon Sessions, included Mason Jr. asking Swift how she prefers to build production around her lyrics and storytelling to create the “right mood and vibe.”

“I was really excited to bring it in and I played them this really, really sad ballad and I was like I think just no drums and they’re like, ‘What if it’s dubstep?'” she recalled. “I was like I don’t know, guys. Let’s give it a run. I don’t know.”

Swift explained that in the end, it “ended up being the best thing for it, and I think as a collaborator, my favorite people to be in the room with are ‘Yes, and?’ people. So why not try it. If they heard it and they thought dubstep, and I came to them specifically because I didn’t want to be making lateral moves creatively, why wouldn’t we go down that path? Why wouldn’t we? I really think that enthusiasm in the studio, it can really make or break what you end up creating.”

highlights.title: In Japan's Niigata Prefecture, the Ancient Culinary Tradition of Fermentation Is Very Much Alive
highlights.summary: From prized sake to pickled potato salad and snow-aged ham, here's how to sip and savor your way through a part of the country known for its fermented foods.
body: My first stop was Willow House, a café and bakery where washi lanterns cast gentle light onto the natural-wood interiors and jazz seeps from the speakers. It's part of the Suzu Group, a coterie of restaurants, izakayas, and guesthouses that have put a modern spin on Niigata's ancient culinary craft. The bakery churns out a rotation of sourdough breads, caramelized apple rolls, and gratin toast with dashi-infused béchamel, while the café has a snack menu featuring miso pickled potato salad, fermented summer tomato salsa, and snow-aged ham.

I continued the tour with a skewer of rice dumplings coated in a sticky-sweet fermented soy sauce glaze at the takeaway counter of Eguchi Dango, a historic fourth-generation wagashi sweets shop. Next is a visit to the Settaya 6th Avenue Fermentation Museum Komegura, located in the former warehouse of a “saffron sake” brewery. Its exterior is decorated with colorful Chinese zodiac panels, while inside is a lab with exhibits on fermentation and a café. Its gift shop sells miso; amazake, a nutritious rice-and-koji drink known for its alleged longevity benefits; and bottles of saffron liqueur made from a recipe that was patented in 1884.

highlights.title: Bitdefender VPN Review: Fast and Affordable Privacy
highlights.summary: Bitdefender VPN has an excellent starting price, even if it lacks the advanced features that privacy nerds may want.
body: The internet is thick with VPN services. So thick, in fact, that it can feel a bit suspicious—and send you running back toward more familiar companies. Bitdefender takes advantage of that with a solid, easy-to-use VPN that offers a great deal on the first year of service. Bitdefender VPN isn’t geared toward the most privacy conscious users, but it does the job if you want a VPN to get around geo-location barriers or browse securely on open Wi-FI networks.

Bitdefender technically offers a free VPN option, but it’s limited. The software heavily pushes you toward a subscription (you’d likely not even realize a free option exists unless you back out of several prompts). Free users can only access automatically selected servers and are capped at 200 MB of data per day.

It’s not clear what price Trump paid for the shares, but by that point they had fallen from their highs of over $200. SpaceX shares were trading in the mid-$150 range on June 23. At the end of trading on Monday, shares closed at the IPO price of $135, possibly putting the president’s stake underwater.

Trump and Musk are close, despite a brief falling out last summer that involved the businessman accusing the president of withholding the Department of Justice’s files on Jeffrey Epstein because of how often Trump’s name appears in them. SpaceX has been hoovering up an increasing amount of government contracts and benefiting from the Trump administration’s deregulatory stance, according to a recent Wall Street Journal analysis.

highlights.title: RFK Jr. may upend how vaccine recommendations are categorized
highlights.summary: Under anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the US health department is considering changing how vaccine recommendations are categorized and described. The move creates the possibility that vaccinations currently considered "routine" or "universal" could be given new designations…
body: Kennedy has made no new rules or recommendations for the categories yet. However, he laid out ideas and possibilities in a Request for Information (RFI) posted online Friday and published in the Federal Register on Monday. In the 10-page document, Kennedy poses questions about the current categories and asks the public to weigh in on ideas for how to change or replace them. The deadline to comment on the questions and ideas is September 20.

Currently, there are three categories of vaccination recommendations granted by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, which is informed by a panel of independent expert advisors, the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP). The three categories are: routine, otherwise considered universal (a recommendation that everyone should get a vaccine); risk-based recommendations (only certain groups at higher risk should get a vaccine); and recommendations based on "shared clinical decision-making," or SCDM (a flexible but uncommon recommendation for vaccination based on the characteristics, values, and preferences of a patient and the judgment of their healthcare provider).

highlights.title: How to encourage smarter AI use in the classroom
highlights.summary: This article is from Making AI Work, MIT Technology Review’s limited-run newsletter examining how to apply LLMs across industries. To receive it in your inbox, sign up here. Chatbots took many schools by surprise upon their release a few years ago.
body: Nevertheless, the generative AI boom increased the burden on teachers, who were already working long hours to plan lessons, make homework assignments, and grade exams, and now needed to adapt to a new technology. For many, it still feels like there’s no clear path forward. Organizations ranging from OpenAI to UNESCO encourage AI use in the classroom, but many teachers feel confused about how exactly to handle it.

Cheshire Academy is a private boarding and day school in Connecticut with about 400 students in grades 9 through 12. Administrators there don’t force instructors to use AI at all, though the school’s librarian and technology coordinator George Aiello claims the “vast majority” of instructors use it in some way. The educators there are trying a patchwork of programs, including general-purpose chatbots like ChatGPT and Perplexity as well as more specialized tools like MagicSchool, an AI-powered platform meant specifically for educators.

Another Dragon Ball theme park is just one of Saudi Arabia's many forays into sports and entertainment as an attempt to launder its public image via " sportswashing." highlights.title: Can You Kill Salmonella in Eggs Without Cooking Them? I Tried It
highlights.summary: With advice from infectious disease experts, I tested a low-effort way to pasteurize eggs at home.
body: It may finally be safe to eat lettuce again after June’s horrifying—and bagged-salad-trust-destroying —cyclospora outbreak. But the summer of ’26’s foodborne illness train rolls on with a new rash of recalls: for salmonella.

The FDA has reported multi-state salmonella bacteria outbreaks tied to jalapeños, granola, dog food, alfalfa sprouts (also featuring E. coli), and something most people probably have in their refrigerator at this very minute: eggs.

Though the eggs being recalled are only from one supplier, Midwest Poultry Services, they were sold under five brand names, including two distributed by one of the country’s largest grocery chains: Kroger and Simple Truth. While this July recall only concerned Kroger stores in Texas, why wait for the next one?

With the advice of two infectious disease experts, I tested what may be the easiest, most universally applicable way to ensure the eggs in your refrigerator are salmonella-free and safe to use—even in raw or near-raw preparations like Hollandaise and pasta carbonara. All it requires is an immersion circulator, a pot of water, and about an hour and a half of your day.

highlights.summary: Steal a Brainrot is so 2025. These days, the most popular game on Roblox is Steal an Egg — but the pet simulator is getting attention for all the wrong reasons. It's one of the most dystopian things ever released on Roblox and is being likened to one of the more depressing episodes of Netflix's…
body: As the name implies, Steal an Egg is an experience where players collect and raise eggs. Hatched eggs turn into pets that generate money every second of their existence, with rarer animals earning more cash than typical monsters. Most players start humbly, with a small chicken — but with enough progress, fans can raise fantastical creatures like dragons. All players have a base, and much like Steal a Brainrot, other people on the server can run away with your assets. Players can also gain eggs by stealing them from various biomes across the map. Each biome has a guardian; the better the egg, the harder it is to steal.

The primary thing that determines success here is speed. Speed can be purchased with real-world money, or it can be upgraded manually by running on a treadmill. Treadmills have a built-in feature called Reels that allows users to watch videos to help pass the time. Screenshots showing this mechanic in action are currently going viral on social media, where shocked onlookers are calling Steal an Egg 's treadmill mechanic dystopian. Many of those screenshots stem from a YouTube video uploaded by a user called Foltyn that generated 1.3 million views on the video platform.

highlights.title: Clash Royale research finds 85% of rage quitters enjoy gaming more after returning
highlights.summary: Supercell has revealed that 85.1% of rage quitters say they enjoy gaming more when they come back. That's according to research commissioned by Clash Royale, which surveyed 9,000 gamers across seven markets as the mobile game searches for a player to become its first-ever rage emote.... [ MORE ]
body: The research found that Mexico had the highest share of players who enjoyed the game more after returning from a rage quit, at 90.5%, while Germany recorded the lowest at 74.4%.

Globally, gamers said they rage quit because they want to do well (31.1%), care about the game (22.1%) and want to protect a winning streak (21.9%). Brazil had the highest share of gamers who had rage quit, at 77%, compared with 59% in Mexico.

The research also found that close to four in 10 gamers who rage quit have done so somewhere public. The US was the only market where gamers wanted an audience, with 55.6% of US rage quitters saying they would happily post a clip of the moment.
In the UK, 31.5% of public rage quitters had done so in a pub, while British gamers also led in ranting to a friend at 20.8% and screaming into a pillow at 17.2%.

highlights.title: 7 Stylish Ways to Wear a Barn Jacket This Fall
highlights.summary: A Fashion Week mainstay—from New York to Copenhagen—the barn jacket is a beloved transitional staple. Here are 7 ways to wear it, plus the best styles to shop.
body: Championed on the runways at Prada, Toteme, and The Row—and spotted at nearly every fashion week, from New York to Copenhagen—the barn jacket remains the ultimate transitional staple. While men’s barn jackets originated in the ’20s as utilitarian workwear, they’ve since been adopted for everyday use, becoming a fixture in the wardrobes of everyone from the British royal family to Gigi Hadid and Zoë Kravitz.

The jacket’s signature design details—a boxy silhouette, multiple pockets, button or snap closures, leather or corduroy collar, and durable, often waxed fabric—make it perfectly practical, but also give it that distinct no-fuss, unpretentious appeal. Its simplicity and versatility are akin to that of a great pair of blue jeans.
